subject: INDG
title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
description: The focus is on Indigenous experience in Canada, but encourages comparative approaches. Introduction to the social, political, economic and cultural dimensions of Indigenous life in Canada.

subject: INDG
title: Topics in Indigenous Studies 1
description: Drawing upon and introducing the burgeoning field of Indigenous Studies, this course is designed to be an introduction to selected themes and topics in Indigenous Studies. Possible examples: Indigenous health, Haudenosaunne culture etc. Topics vary from year to year.
notes: Supplementary Calendar Info: INDG 202 and INDG 300 are NOT a sequence of courses.

subject: INDG
title: Topics in Indigenous Studies 2
description: This course is designed to examine specific themes and topics in Indigenous Studies. Possible examples: Haudenosaunee governance etc. Topics vary from year to year.
notes: Supplementary Calendar Info: INDG 202 and INDG 300 are NOT a sequence of courses.

subject: INDG
title: Indigenous Contemporary Resistance
description: In-depth and experiential examination of contemporary Indigenous resistance movements based on Indigenous worldviews and land-based knowledge.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INDG 202 when topic was "Contemporary Indigenous Resistance".

subject: INDG
title: Introduction to Kanien’kéha 1
description: Foundations of the Kanien'kéha language and Haudenosaunee worldviews, including reading and speaking basic Kanien'kéha, using key words and phrases to communicate basic needs, and the verb-based morphology and grammatical structure of the language.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INDG 202 when topic was "Introduction to Kanien'ké:ha".

subject: INDG
title: Introduction to Kanien’kéha 2
description: Additional study of the foundations of the Kanien'kéha language and Haudenosaunee worldviews, including reading and speaking basic Kanien'kéha, using key words and phrases to communicate basic needs, and the verb-based morphology and grammatical structure of the language.

prerequisites.text: INDG 302 or permission of the department.

notes: Students who already have some proficiency in Kanien'kéha should speak with the instructor.

subject: INDG
title: Seminar: Indigenous Studies
description: This advanced course is designed to examine specific topics and themes in Indigenous Studies. Possible examples: Indigenous research methodologies. Topics vary from year to year.

subject: INDG
title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Indigenous Studies
description: The focus is on Indigenous experience in Canada, but encourages comparative approaches.Capstone seminar course offering an in-depth focus on one or more issues in Indigenous Studies.

subject: INDG
title: Indigenous Food Sovereignty
description: Examination of food sovereignty as it relates to First Nation, Inuit, and Métis and their connection to the land as sustenance. The focus is on natural food sources and practices.

restrictions.text: Not open to students who have taken INDG 400 when the topic was “Indigenous Food Sovereignty”.

subject: INDG
title: Rotinonhsón:ni Land-Based Pedagogy
description: The teachings of land, Ohen:ton Karihwátehkwen (Words before all Else) as well as stories that engage in the multiple tenets of Indigenous land-based education. Land-based practices and Indigenous literature. Participation is based on the values of Skén’nen (peace), Kahsatsténhsera (united strength), Ka'nikonhrí:io (good mind).

prerequisites.text: Required INDG 200, INDG 401 is recommended but not required.

restrictions.text: Open to students in the Indigenous Studies Program or with permission of the instructor

notes: This is an intensive summer field course.
